content: Before using the medication, squeeze the container to check for leaks. If the container leaks, discard the solution immediately. For optimal effectiveness, administer this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. To help maintain consistency, use the medication at the same time(s) every day. Continue using the medication for the entire prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Learn proper techniques for storing and discarding needles and medical supplies safely. Common side effects may include swelling, redness, pain, or soreness at the injection site. Rarely, this medication may cause loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or headache. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. In rare cases, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to the bacteria Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has ended. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using cefotetan, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins, penicillins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages while taking this medication and for at least three days after completing it. Cefotetan may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. This medication can pass into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine glucose tests or serum/urine creatinine tests, potentially causing false results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. Laboratory and/or medical tests, such as complete blood counts and kidney function tests, may be conducted while you are using this product. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Different brands or packaging of this medication may have varying storage requirements. Refer to the product package for specific storage instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is important to note that this summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
